newsitem.title: FRANCE: Netanyahu flies to Germany, denies curtailing tour.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu flies to Germany, denies curtailing tour.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu left Paris for Germany on Thursday insisting he will complete a European tour despite a crisis at home sparked by bloody clashes between Palestinians and police.
Officials at Orly airport south of the French capital said his flight took off at 6.55 a.m. (0455 GMT) for Hanover on the final leg of his tour.
Netanyahu had earlier denied that he was planning to curtail his schedule.
"The reports that he is coming home early are without foundation," a spokesman for Netanyahu told reporters accompanying the prime minister.
In Washington, a State Department spokesman had said he believed Netanyahu intended to curtail his tour because of the violence, in which seven Arabs died on Wednesday.

The Israeli prime minister, who has visited Britain and France on his tour, was due to visit the former Nazi concentration camp at Bergen-Belsen in Germany before going on to Bonn for talks with Chancellor Helmut Kohl.
He was due to leave for Israel on Thursday night.
